gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in named lab discharge tests the BLUETTI AC180 delivered 980–1,030 Wh of AC energy (Outdoor Life, StorageReview), more than the EcoFlow DELTA 3 / DELTA 3 Plus (900–910 Wh), the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (910 Wh, OutdoorGearLab) and the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (850 Wh, Notebookcheck). It also does not state that on a ~34 W overnight-style load these ~1 kWh stations gave only about half their rating (530–620 Wh, Outdoor Life).
standout_why: I compared against powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (cited), voltandvalley.com, trek4tech.com and our own kit page. PowerSized says it has not tested any unit and assumes 85% usable capacity and 75% panel output. Its one outside figure is OutdoorGearLab's general finding that 12 panels gave 56–91% of their rated watts, which covers part of the panel side but no station. Volt & Valley has no measurements, only manufacturer charge times plus its own 75% and 85% conventions. Trek4Tech says it 'did not test any of these units' and estimates usable Wh without giving a method. None of them gives a measured Wh-delivered figure for any candidate or the low-load collapse. solargenadvisor.com could not be read because the site failed its SSL certificate check.
decides: This backs the BLUETTI AC180 + 2 × 200 W kit as the one that puts the most measured energy into AC loads. Two labs got 980 Wh at ~380 W and 1,030 Wh at 350 W from it. The C1000 Gen 2 gave 850 Wh at 250 W on an EU 230 V unit and the DELTA 3 Plus 910 Wh. That partly offsets the AC180's $1,232 kit price against the DELTA 3 Plus kit at about $1,099–1,119. It weakens the 'lowest price' case for the ALLPOWERS P1800 because no named reviewer has published a full discharge test for it. The low-load result should go on the page as a warning: overnight loads like a CPAP or laptop get about 50–60% of the rated Wh, whichever kit the shopper buys.
candidates: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (+ PS400 at Off-Grid Source)

findings.label: Usable AC energy at ~380 W (dehumidifier)
findings.source_title: The Best Portable Power Stations of 2026, Tested and Reviewed (Outdoor Life, Laura Lancaster, published 2026-01-09)
findings.note: Unit fully charged, run down on a ~380 W dehumidifier, energy logged with a Kill-a-Watt meter. After 3 months stored in a garage it gave 950 Wh (82%). Measured recharge time 1.3 h.

findings.label: Usable AC energy at ~34 W (grow light)
findings.source_title: The Best Portable Power Stations of 2026, Tested and Reviewed (Outdoor Life)
findings.note: The page gives three different percentages for this run: 54% in the table, 39.9% in the report card and 'about 47 percent' in the text. 620 / 1,152 = 54%. Use the Wh figure, not the percentage.

findings.label: Usable AC energy at 350 W; wall energy to recharge
findings.value: 1,030 Wh out; 1,360 Wh from the wall for 0–100%
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC180 Portable Power Station Review (StorageReview, Kevin OBrien, 2023-05-26)
findings.note: 1,030 / 1,152 = 89%. Round-trip 1,030 / 1,360 = 76%. No measured solar input reported.

findings.label: Usable energy 100→0%; wall energy to recharge
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus Review (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty, 2025-01-02)
findings.note: The review does not state the discharge load. It measured UPS transfer at just over 8 ms against EcoFlow's 10 ms and an app-shown charge rate of 1.45 kW. No measured solar input.

findings.label: Efficiency at high load; AC full-charge time
findings.value: 82% over a 32-minute run at 1,573 W; full charge from empty in 55 min
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus Review (The Solar Lab, undated, no author named)
findings.note: Says it got 'really close to' 1,000 W combined solar input using two Serious 415 W bifacial panels but gives no exact reading, so that is left out as a figure.

findings.label: Usable AC energy at ~380 W and ~34 W
findings.value: 900 Wh (88%) at ~380 W; 530 Wh over 13.9 h (52%) at ~34 W; 860 Wh (84%) after 3 months' storage
findings.source_title: The Best Portable Power Stations of 2026, Tested and Reviewed (Outdoor Life)
findings.note: This is the DELTA 3, not the DELTA 3 Plus in our kit row. Same Kill-a-Watt method as the AC180 rows. Measured recharge time 55 min.

findings.label: Usable AC energy at ~250 W; wall energy to charge; noise
findings.value: 850 Wh (83%); 1,110 Wh in (about 92% vs 1,024 Wh); about 45 dB at 1 m
findings.source_title: Lighter, stronger and faster but... Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 power station review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, published 2025-12-21, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Tested on the EU 230 V version and run to the 1% cutoff. The US 120 V unit may differ. AC charge took just under 55 min without Boost. Noise measured at high output and fast charging. No solar measurement.
